data.title: Prediction markets give Bitcoin a 2% shot at $200,000 in 2026, a record low
data.description:
Traders on prediction markets now give Bitcoin just a 2% chance of reaching $200,000 in 2026, a record low for those contracts.

On Kalshi, the contract asking whether Bitcoin will trade above $200,000 by January 1, 2027, was priced at 2% as of October 2026. Polymarket tells a similar story, with odds for the same milestone sitting somewhere between less than 1% and 2%.

The Polymarket figure is down from around 4%.

These particular contracts settle against the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index, a benchmark price feed for Bitcoin.

Bitcoin was trading near $82,000 to $84,000 in early October 2026, so reaching $200,000 would require the price to more than double before the calendar flips.

Contracts betting Bitcoin hits $90,000 carry a 63% implied probability. The $100,000 contract sits at 28% odds.

Further up the ladder, contracts covering the $150,000 to $190,000 range are trading in the single digits.

Total volume across the related Polymarket contracts exceeds $74 million.

Data from September already showed the $200,000 contract priced at 2%, suggesting expectations had cooled well before October arrived. Polymarket's slide from around 4% to its current range shows traders steadily trimming their bets on an aggressive rally rather than panic-selling them.

data.title: Are you an NRI renting out property in India? Here is who can help to manage it; how to pay tax and remit money abroad
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Non-resident Indians (NRIs) can legally own and rent out property in India, whether it is a family home they inherited, an investment flat they have purchased or a house they chose to keep after moving abroad.

Renting out such property can provide a steady income while also ensuring that it remains occupied and maintained.

However, managing a rental property from abroad can be challenging, particularly when it comes to handling tenants and repairs, collecting rent, completing documentation and complying with tax rules.

Here is what NRI property owners need to know about managing rent, getting professional assistance and repatriating rental income.

An NRI can let out their property in India by using online rent agreements, digital tenant verification, e-stamping and a non-resident ordinary (NRO) bank account for rent collection, which can be further remitted abroad.

Tenants can transfer the rent amount through NEFT, IMPS, or UPI linked to the NRO account. Many landlords also set up automatic reminders or use a property manager to follow up on payment dates.

Funds in an NRO account are partially repatriable up to $1 million per financial year, subject to applicable conditions and payment of taxes where required. The house owner must also keep rent collection consistent and documented to make the repatriation process easier.

Many people may wonder if they can receive rent in their non-resident external (NRE) account instead as funds maintained in it can be fully repatriated outside India. However, Indian residents cannot make direct payments or deposit local funds into a NRE account.

In the event the tenant is an NRI or a person of Indian origin (PIO), only then the landlord can receive rent for immovable property in their NRE account, according to a blog post by ICICI Bank.

NRIs have several options for managing rental property in India, depending on how much assistance they need and how frequently they can oversee the property themselves.

A trusted family member or friend can handle basic tasks like coordinating with tenants, handing over keys and arranging repairs. Such a representative can be appointed through a Power of Attorney (POA) to carry out specified legal and administrative tasks on the NRI's behalf.

Alternatively, a property management company can handle day-to-day responsibilities, including finding tenants, collecting rent and coordinating maintenance. This option can be considered if you cannot appoint a POA or need professional assistance.

Some NRIs combine these options. For instance, a property manager may handle daily operations, while a POA holder signs the rent agreement or completes other formalities that require the owner's authorisation.

Rental income earned by a non-resident Indian (NRI) from property in India is taxable under the head 'Income from house property' at the applicable income-tax slab rates. NRIs can claim a deduction for municipal taxes paid during the financial year, along with the standard deduction of 30% of the net annual value, while calculating taxable rental income.

Under Section 195 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, rent paid to an NRI is generally subject to Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) at the applicable rates, including surcharge and cess, wherever applicable. The final tax liability depends on the individual's taxable income and the applicable tax provisions.

As an NRI, you may also consult your tax advisor to analyse relevant Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) to claim any benefit on such rental income available under such agreement.

data.title: Sam Altman-backed Bitcoin life insurer, Meanwhile, raises more funds
data.description:
Meanwhile, a life insurer licensed to operate completely in Bitcoin, announced $37.5 million in new funding from existing investors.

Bermuda-based Meanwhile, whose backers include OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, has now raised more than $180 million.

Bain Capital Crypto led the new round, alongside Haun Ventures, Framework Ventures, Pantera Capital, Apollo, Northwestern Mutual Future Ventures, and Morgan Creek Digital, it said in a statement.

The round follows increased international demand for Meanwhile’s Bitcoin life insurance policies, particularly in Asia, Europe and the Middle East, amid broader macro instability, according to the statement.

“Wealthy families around the world already hold Bitcoin. What they haven’t had is a regulated way to pass it on,” Zac Townsend, Meanwhile’s co-founder and CEO, said in the statement. “Brokers came to us because their clients kept asking. This round lets us keep up with them.”

Passing Bitcoin to the next generation

In early 2026, Meanwhile launched BTC Life 1-Pay, a single-premium whole life policy built for high-net-worth clients outside the United States. It is the company’s second product line after BTC 10-Pay, which is designed for US taxpayers.

Policies can be owned by individuals, trusts or companies, which makes them a fit for succession and estate planning, the company said.

Net long-term underwriting income has already passed last year’s total and is on track to more than double in 2026, the company added, without revealing precise figures.

Cointelegraph reported in June that WTW, a global insurance broker and risk advisory company, had acquired crypto insurance platform Redefind and launched a digital asset protection service that covers expenses related to forensic investigations, asset tracing and legal recovery efforts following theft or loss.

Redefind is a crypto insurance platform that allows individuals and institutions to purchase coverage for digital assets held across different custody arrangements. The company said its system uses cryptographic proof of ownership to verify insured assets.

data.title: RBI opens oil dollar window, tightens forex trades to arrest rupee slide
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has opened a special dollar window for state-run oil companies to meet their dollar requirements on daily basis and tightened foreign exchange derivative rules to ease pressure on the rupee and curb volatility. The measures could provide near-term relief, but are unlikely to reverse the currency’s broader depreciation trend, market participants said.

The rupee closed at 96.73 against the dollar on October 9, near its record low of 96.96 touched in May. It has depreciated by more than 7 percent in calendar 2026 and around 3.5 percent in FY27 so far, amid elevated crude prices, a strong dollar, high global bond yields and weak capital flows.

With the rupee nearing its record low, the RBI appears keen to prevent it from breaching the psychologically significant 97-per-dollar mark, where further weakness could intensify corporate dollar-buying and speculative short positions. Traders have reported stepped-up dollar-selling intervention by state-run banks as the currency moves past 96.80.

The RBI has lowered the threshold for certain forex derivative transactions without an underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million, restricted the rebooking of cancelled rupee-linked contracts and introduced a cash reserve requirement for specified transactions.

Oil window could ease spot-market pressure

Crude oil accounts for around 25 percent of India’s imports. Routing oil companies’ daily dollar requirements through the special window could shift some demand away from the spot market, although the dollars supplied will come from the RBI’s foreign exchange reserves.

A treasury head at a private bank said the measure could ease spot-market pressure, while the derivative restrictions could moderate forward premiums.

“The oil window should help reduce some of the pressure on the spot market, given that crude oil accounts for around 25 percent of India’s imports. The restrictions on derivative transactions could also ease pressure on forward premiums in the near term,” the treasury head at a private bank said.

“The lower threshold for transactions without an underlying exposure would mainly affect positions not backed by a genuine transaction.” Importers hedging actual payment obligations should not be affected in the same way.

“These measures could provide near-term relief to both the spot rupee and forward premiums. But the underlying pressures remain. India’s balance of payments is still weak, the dollar is strong and global bond yields are elevated, an adverse combination for an emerging market that is a net oil importer,” the treasury head said, adding that medium-term depreciation risks would persist.

Dilip Parmar, Research Analyst at HDFC Securities, said the measures were aimed at curbing volatility and speculative positions.

“The RBI is looking to curb excessive volatility and speculative positions, while the special dollar window will move part of the oil companies’ demand away from the spot market. The measures should support the rupee, but banks may pass on the additional hedging costs to customers,” Parmar said.

Derivative rules tighten

The RBI has tightened forex derivative rules by lowering the limit for transactions without an underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million. It has also barred the rebooking of cancelled rupee-linked contracts, while allowing rollovers at maturity, and introduced a cash reserve requirement of 20 percent of the notional value for specified derivative contracts exceeding $2 million.

The measures aim to curb speculative positions and volatility, though the additional reserve requirement could raise hedging costs for customers. requirement applies to contracts used to hedge current-account exposures where the user buys foreign currency against the rupee. The additional cost could be passed on to customers through higher hedging charges.

Earlier interventions and falling reserves

During the 2013 rupee crisis, the RBI tightened liquidity, restricted certain currency positions and opened a special dollar-swap window for oil marketing companies. It also introduced a swap facility to attract foreign currency deposits from non-resident Indians.

In February 2018, the RBI raised the limit for exchange-traded currency derivative positions without an underlying exposure to $100 million. In March 2026, it capped banks’ net open dollar-rupee positions at $100 million and restricted authorised dealers from offering non-deliverable forwards to clients to curb arbitrage between onshore and offshore markets. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said in April that the restrictions were temporary.

The latest measures come as foreign exchange reserves have declined. Reserves fell by $18.34 billion to $757.46 billion in the week ended September 25 and by another $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in the week ended October 2.

The combined decline of around $31.3 billion over two weeks leaves reserves about $51.1 billion below the record high of $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4. RBI dollar sales may have contributed, although valuation changes in foreign currency assets and gold also affect the headline figure.

At the October 7 monetary policy press conference, Malhotra said the rupee could be undervalued based on measures such as the real effective exchange rate. “Markets can be quite irrational in the short run,” he said, adding that the RBI would work to ensure the currency stabilised and moved in an orderly manner.

Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury at Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP, said the measures should be temporary.

“The Governor has already said that the rupee is undervalued and that the RBI would take all steps to bring it back to its fair value. These measures should be temporary,” Bhansali said. He added that the rupee could recover towards 94.50-95 per dollar, which he considers closer to fair value.

Separately, the RBI has scheduled an open market sale of government securities worth Rs 25,000 crore for October 13 to absorb surplus liquidity. From the fortnight beginning October 16, banks must maintain at least 99 percent of their prescribed cash reserve ratio (CRR) on a daily basis, up from 90 percent earlier. The change affects daily maintenance against banks’ net demand and time liabilities (NDTL), not the prescribed CRR ratio itself.

data.title: SpaceX’s Wireless Ambitions Could Be A Windfall For CCI — Bernstein Analyst Calls It the ‘Best Beneficiary’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rezaei said the SpaceX deal could effectively introduce a new carrier to an industry that has long relied on three major customers: AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon.
  • She added that this could be significant because the economics of the tower business become increasingly attractive as additional carriers lease space on existing infrastructure.
  • Rezaei said that SpaceX's push into wireless could demonstrate that satellite connectivity and terrestrial networks are complementary rather than competing technologies.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) is making a bigger push into the wireless business, and Wall Street is already trying to figure out which companies could benefit most from the move.

During an interview with CNBC, Bernstein senior analyst Madison Rezaei highlighted a potentially unexpected group of winners, which are the companies that own the towers supporting America's cellular networks.

SpaceX shares gained more than 1% during the regular trading session, and rose 0.1% further in the after-hours trade. Shares of Crown Castle Inc. (CCI) soared nearly 16% in the regular session, and edged up by 0.1% in the afterhours trade.

SpaceX Could Add A New Customer To Cell Towers

Rezaei said the SpaceX deal could effectively introduce a new carrier to an industry that has long relied on three major customers: AT&T Inc. (T), T-Mobile US Inc. (TMUS) and Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ).

"We suddenly have a new carrier on the tower companies," Rezaei said.

She added that this could be significant because the economics of the tower business become increasingly attractive as additional carriers lease space on existing infrastructure.

"Once you've built up the tower, every incremental tenant that you add is very, very profitable," Rezaei said.

According to Rezaei, the potential addition of SpaceX as a customer could translate into a roughly 10%-15% increase in recurring revenue for tower companies.

The key question, however, is which tower operator is best positioned to capture that opportunity.

Rezaei Explains Why CCI Could Be The Biggest Winner

Rezaei pointed to Crown Castle Inc. (CCI) as the strongest beneficiary of SpaceX's wireless ambitions, largely because of its exposure to the U.S. market.

"Crown is the best beneficiary today," Rezaei said.

Unlike American Tower Corp. (AMT) and SBA Communications Corp. (SBAC), which have significant international operations, Crown Castle is a U.S.-only pure play.

"Crown is pure-play U.S., so they're just proportionately rewarded here," Rezaei said.

Rezaei currently has a $96 price target on Crown Castle and a $214 target on American Tower.

SPCX May Actually Be Validating The Cell Tower Model, Says Rezaei

Rezaei argues SpaceX's latest move into wireless points to the opposite of what investors have feared for years. Rather than undermining traditional terrestrial wireless infrastructure, Starlink's expansion could reinforce the need for cell towers, she said.

“Towers have been extremely depressed,” Rezaei said, pointing to concerns that satellite technology could eventually “eat terrestrial wireless networks.”

“I think the clear answer here is no,” she said.

Instead, SpaceX's push into wireless could demonstrate that satellite connectivity and terrestrial networks are complementary rather than competing technologies, Rezaei added.

“To us, this is sort of a signal that SpaceX is really endorsing the fact that you need terrestrial wireless networks for mobile to work,” she explained.

There is still a major question hanging over the opportunity: whether SpaceX ultimately builds its own terrestrial network.

Rezaei said there are three potential paths for SpaceX: it could build its own network, partner with an existing wireless carrier or potentially acquire another company.

Of those options, she believes a carrier partnership is the most likely, although the major wireless operators have so far been reluctant to give SpaceX the deal it wants.

"So what we're all trying to do is, like, a probability weighting of: are they going to build?" Rezaei said.

What Retail Investors Think Of CCI Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Crown Castle trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

SPCX stock is up 8% year-to-date, while CCI stock is down 10%. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 14% over the past 12 months, while the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) is up 16%.

data.title: Bitcoin slides toward $82.5K as over $2.4 billion in crypto liquidations hit longs
data.description:
Over $2.4 billion in crypto positions were liquidated this week as Bitcoin fell from $85.7K to $82.5K. Most of the damage landed on traders betting the price would go up.

The sell-off arrived during a rough stretch for markets in general, with bond yields climbing, oil getting expensive and money leaving Bitcoin ETFs.

In early October 2026, Bitcoin dropped from near $86,600 to intraday lows of approximately $80,350.

Bitcoin pulled back from highs near $87,350 to lows of approximately $80,350–$82,900, depending on the session.

By October 9–10, the price had partly recovered to around $82,500.

Individual 24-hour sessions saw between $696 million and over $1.2 billion in positions wiped out. Added up across the week, the total cleared $2 billion. The figure in the original report puts it at over $2.4 billion.

Long positions made up roughly 85%-93% of liquidations over several days. In single sessions, the forced closures hit somewhere between 100,000 and 180,000 traders.

The broader market felt it too. Total crypto market capitalization dropped roughly $110 billion within 36 hours during the downturn.

US Treasury yields climbed upwards of 5.3% during the period, while oil prices moved above $101 per barrel.

US spot Bitcoin ETF flows also turned negative. On peak days, the outflows ran into the hundreds of millions of dollars.

On-chain data added another uncomfortable signal. Short-term holders reportedly sent 55,600 BTC to exchanges at a loss during the decline.

Open interest, the total value of outstanding futures and derivatives positions, barely moved and held steady near $150 billion.

It also invites comparison with the last big wipeout. In October 2025, a liquidation event erased $19 billion in positions.

Technical levels sit around $82,500, with clusters between $81,000 and $84,000. Bitcoin's partial recovery landed right on that $82,500 line.

data.title: Skill development Ministry felicitates 'Team India' for historic WorldSkills Shanghai performance
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship hosted a felicitation ceremony for Team India's young competitors following their historic performance at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, where India secured its first-ever position among the world's top 10, finishing 10th globally with six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence.

Speaking to ANI in Delhi on Friday, Chairman of Jindal Steel & Power Limited (JSPL), Naveen Jindal, expressed delight at India's performance and said he was confident that the country would do even better in the next edition of the competition.

"I feel absolutely thrilled at India's performance at the World Skills Competition in Shanghai. I was there with my wife to see them perform, to cheer them. I was really happy that they did so well... India did so well, and we moved up from the last competition, where we were ranked 13 all over. Now we moved up to the 10th rank." Jindal said.

Smriti Nambiar, India's 'Best of the Nation' awardee and a silver medallist at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, spoke about the overwhelming support she received after the competition and her experience of meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Speaking to ANI, Nambiar said, "The amount of love and support I've received after the competition has been so overwhelming. It's not every day you can say that you had the opportunity to meet the Prime Minister. It was really amazing that he took the time to come out and speak to us and really give that stage to the skills that we deserve. The kindness and patience with which he interacted with us were really lovely."

WorldSkills Shanghai silver medallist Mehrunissa Begum also described meeting the Prime Minister as an amazing experience, saying the interaction made the competitors feel comfortable and gave them an opportunity to share their ideas and listen to his experiences.

"It's an amazing experience. I am still recovering from the high of the medal and winning at WorldSkills. Also, today we met the Prime Minister, and that was an amazing experience, to be honest. We felt comfortable around him and felt really very comfortable giving all the ideas and listening to his experiences as well. It was wonderful," Begum told ANI.

The felicitation ceremony was also attended by Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the Minister of State for Education and senior officials of the Government of India.

Earlier on Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with the representatives of Team India at the WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026, at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, on Friday.

During the interaction, the participants shared their experiences during the competition. They expressed pride in representing their country at the world stage. The participants discussed adapting to new tools, software, technical systems and work processes during the international competition. They also spoke about the work being done by the government towards skill development, which is helping youth.

Prime Minister congratulated the participants for representing India on the global stage. He urged them to become ambassadors of skill development. He said that practical skills are as important as academic degrees.

WorldSkills is the world's leading international skills competition, bringing together young professionals from participating countries and regions to demonstrate excellence across a wide range of vocational and technical skills.

WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, the 48th WorldSkills Competition, was held from September 22 to 27, 2026, at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai. Team India secured 10th position at the 48th WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026, winning 6 Silver Medals and 20 Medals for Excellence. India was represented by its largest-ever contingent of 70 competitors participating across 63 skills.

The interaction was also attended by Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the Minister of State for Education and senior officials of the Government of India.

data.title: Reserve Bank of India opens special dollar window for state-run oil marketing companies
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) opens a designated foreign exchange window to fulfill the complete daily dollar requirements of state-run oil refiners, according to an official statement issued by the central bank.

The intervention applies specifically to three public sector oil marketing companies: Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited, and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited.

"On the basis of assessment of current market conditions, Reserve Bank of India has decided to open a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs)," the central bank stated in its document.

The facility will begin operations from October 12, 2026, which falls on a Monday, and will continue to operate until further notice, the central bank confirmed.

Under the operational framework, the central bank will conduct sales of US dollars to these state refiners via designated banks rather than direct open-market bidding by the fuel retailers.

"Under the facility, the Reserve Bank will undertake sale of USD to the public sector OMCs through designated bank/s," the RBI stated.

The decision follows the central bank's internal review and evaluation of prevailing conditions in the currency and financial markets.

"The facility will come in effect from October 12, 2026 (Monday) and will remain in place until further notice," the Reserve Bank added in the statement.

The designated mechanism covers all foreign exchange requirements needed on a daily basis by Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited, and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited.

The institutional arrangement channels their foreign currency demand entirely through authorized dealer banks designated for the transactions.

data.title: Opposition conspiring to erode faith in democracy with foreign support: Shivraj Singh Chouhan on CJP protest
data.description:
Bhopal, Oct. 10 -- Hailing the National Democratic Alliance's (NDA) performance in the recent by-elections, Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Saturday launched a scathing attack on the opposition, accusing it of attempting to unleash "anarchy on the streets" with the backing of "foreign powers" after failing to win the public's trust at the ballot box.

Chouhan asserted that the electorate has reaffirmed its faith in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of a developed nation.

"In yesterday's by-elections, whether in Bengal, Assam, or Puducherry, the BJP and NDA achieved a magnificent victory. The public mandate has made it clear: the people are saying that our resolve is to build a developed India, and we will do it. We are determined to achieve it and will continue to do so," Chouhan said.

Targeting the opposition parties, the Union Minister alleged that their persistent electoral defeats have driven them to undermine democratic institutions.

"On one hand, the public stands with PM Modi for development and the creation of a developed India; on the other, the opposition is frustrated and despondent. They cannot win in the electoral arena or earn the public's trust. Consequently, they are attempting to spread anarchy on the streets, undermining constitutional institutions, conspiring to erode faith in democracy, and tearing the Constitution to shreds," he stated.

He further alleged, "The opposition is not doing this alone; they are acting with the support of foreign forces. However, the public has made its stance clear: we stand with development and with PM Modi."

Reacting sharply to the ongoing demonstrations in the national capital, Chouhan termed the protest a calculated attempt to destabilise the country, taking direct aim at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi.

"This is an attempt to create and spread anarchy, a conspiracy by the opposition. I am appalled by their attitude: showing kindness to outsiders while oppressing their own people. They want anarchy to spread in our country because they cannot win otherwise; they are willing to stoop so low just to gain power," the Union Minister said.

"They resent the progress of our entrepreneurs. Rahul Gandhi supports foreigners; this has become the true character of the Congress and the opposition. It is a conspiracy to weaken the country," Chouhan added.

On a day that various organisations led by the CJP have called for protests against the Election Commission, Delhi Police continued to detain activists after informing them that there was no legal sanction for the protest.'

CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke who was on a flight to Delhi from Mumbai to participate in the protest posted a video on Instagram claiming that Police were detaining him and his associates even as they deboarded the aircraft at Delhi Airport.

In the Video, Dipke is heard alleging," So, you can see that Delhi Police is entering the plane to arrest us. They are all entering the plane. We just landed. All the Delhi Police officers are standing in the aisle. They are trying to arrest us from inside the plane.This is the fear of Not even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency. All we wanted to do is a peaceful protest, and they are picking us up from the flight like we are criminals."

"You can see where the nation is heading. They are here to arrest us directly from the flight. This is something not even Indira Gandhi had done. This is dictatorship, where Delhi Police has entered the flight and is trying to arrest us. Come on, arrest us. We are here to be arrested. Come on, arrest us. We are not afraid of you," Dipke is heard saying.

Delhi Police on Saturday said it had detained around 500 people who arrived in different groups from various locations ahead of the planned protest in the national capital, while nearly 50 people with criminal antecedents were also apprehended as part of preventive measures.

"Around 500 people coming in different groups from various locations have been detained. In addition, nearly 50 anti-social elements with criminal antecedents have been picked up so that they do not disturb the atmosphere or incite trouble," Delhi Police said.

As part of the security arrangements, the New Delhi district has been divided into 20 operational zones, with dedicated detention centres established for each zone, police said.

Several demonstrators were detained after gathering at Jantar Mantar and Sansad Marg amid tight security and extensive barricading across the national capital.

data.title: Brazilian police seize $1.7M in crypto from phishing ring's wallets
data.description:
Brazilian police have pulled US$1,708,534 in crypto out of self-custody wallets linked to a phishing ring. The Civil Police of Santa Catarina (PCSC) seized the funds during Operação ClickFix, which it carried out on September 10, 2026.

It is the largest self-custody digital asset recovery Brazilian civil police have made to date.

The haul was worth approximately R$8.78 million at the time of the seizure. It spread across four assets: Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), TRON (TRX) and Tether (USDT).

Authorities released the details publicly between October 7 and 9, 2026, roughly a month after the operation itself.

The funds moved out of the group's wallets in 13 separate transactions. Investigators relied on blockchain tracing tools from Chainalysis to follow and confirm the transfers.

The assets then landed in an institutional account at Foxbit, a Brazilian exchange, where they now sit under state custody.

Other reports have identified roughly US$218,000 in additional funds. How that amount fits alongside the main seizure figure has not been laid out in the material released so far.

The crypto was only one piece of a larger takedown. The operation produced two arrests and the seizure of luxury vehicles, among them a Corvette valued at more than R$1.5 million.

Courts also ordered freezes on bank accounts totaling up to R$93 million. Another R$5 million in real estate was caught up in the judicial measures.

The group's method gave the operation its name. According to the research findings, the ring used the ClickFix social engineering technique, which helps attackers take over a victim's device and steal credentials.

In a self-custody wallet, the owner holds the private keys directly, with no exchange or bank acting as middleman. When police want to freeze funds sitting on an exchange, they can serve a court order on that company. With self-custody, no company sits in the middle to receive the order, which makes recovering assets considerably harder.

PCSC did not simply ask a platform to freeze an account; it moved funds out of wallets the group itself controlled and into a custodial account under state control. Authorities recovered crucial seed phrases during raids and demonstrated their capacity to import wallets and analyze blockchain data, enabling controlled asset transfers.

The use of Chainalysis tooling shows how Brazilian investigators are approaching these cases. The choice of Foxbit as custodian points to another emerging pattern: seized crypto has to be stored somewhere secure, and here the state leaned on a domestic exchange's institutional infrastructure to hold it.

The research findings frame the seizure as a sign of increasing regulatory scrutiny over self-custody wallets. The wallets in this case were allegedly tied to a criminal operation, and the seizure came alongside arrests and court-ordered freezes, not as a blanket action against ordinary holders.

The findings also note the case may raise awareness of phishing schemes and push investors to strengthen their defenses. Some may look for custodial solutions with stronger security, while others may simply tighten up how they handle their own keys and devices.

Also worth tracking: what ultimately happens to the assets sitting in Foxbit's institutional account, and whether the roughly US$218,000 flagged in other reports gets folded into the official tally.

data.title: Karan Ahuja of Cococart is raising the bar for premium confectionery in India
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Karan Ahuja had been playing pickleball in another part of town before we met at Coco Cafe, the food and beverage (F&B) outlet of Cococart, best known as one of India's leading omnichannel retailers and importers of chocolates, in Mumbai airport's terminal 2. The 35-year-old co-founder of the company is serious about fitness, especially since his job requires him to eat 150 grams of chocolate on an average day.

"I love dark chocolate, but I have to taste a range of products for work," Ahuja says. This occupational hazard means that he can't, in good faith, prevent his toddler daughters from indulging in chocolates either. "They get to eat what they want, though we try to limit it to healthier, 85% dark chocolate."

In 2020, when Ahuja started Cococart with his elder brother Arjun (who has since moved on to other arms of the family's businesses), it was more out of a desperation to make the best of a bad situation rather than as a connoisseur of fine chocolates. His family owned Flemingo International, a flourishing duty-free business, since 2003. By 2019, the company had built its presence in 37 countries, from the Americas to Australia, but then the pandemic hit, and air travel came to a halt worldwide.

"In a year-and-a-half, we had to close about 70% of our group operations," Ahuja says. "Our European business was doing $400 million. We sold it for $4 million. We owned a cruise ship business, which did £200 million, and had to be sold too. " As the family was coming to terms with cultivating a "highly defensive and protectionist" mindset, Atul, Karan's father, had a more immediate concern.

"We had a huge inventory of imported chocolate sitting with us," Karan recalls, "which is different from having liquor and perfume." While the latter could be sold off whenever travel routes opened, items like chocolate have a limited shelf life. Shipments that had arrived in January and February of 2020 were good for six-nine months, after which the entire stock would have to be written off. And so, Ahuja senior told his boys to find a way to sell off the inventory.

As it happened, the family was on the verge of selling Flemingo International when covid-19 broke out. "My dad had already decided on his next venture-distributing imported confectionery in India. He basically planned to build a Nykaa for chocolates," Karan says. "Arjun and I simply stole his idea. That's how Cococart came about."

Funded by the family, the company did business of Rs.6.85 crore in the first year, of which Rs.92.5 lakh was online. Currently backed by the Adani Group, which acquired a 74% stake in it in 2024 (on a deal valued at Rs.200 crore), Cococart closed FY25 at Rs.266 crore. This financial year, Ahuja says, they are likely to hit Rs.350 crore, depending on Diwali sales. The company had Ebitda loss of Rs.2.99 crore in FY26, has a monthly turnaround of Rs.30-31 crore and is expected to become profitable this financial year.

But the numbers don't tell the whole story, especially the roller-coaster ride that the Ahuja family's fortunes have been through in the last two decades.

Atul, a mechanical engineer by training, worked at an IT job for a few years before starting, in 1991, his first business-making chairs and sofas. Not only was he a well-intentioned man, he was also a stickler for compliance, qualities that don't necessarily make a canny businessman. It was only a matter of time before people from the extended family were copying his idea and starting similar ventures. "Since he liked to do everything by the book and pay every tax, dad started getting hugely undercut by his competitors," Karan says. "He had a rough few years before he shut down the business in 2002. By the time I was 11, we had gone bankrupt."

Atul was jobless for a year, before things looked up. Their home in Mumbai's Chembur, where Karan grew up in a joint family, was right next to a bungalow owned by the actor, Raj Kapoor. "I don't know how, but my great-grandfather was friends with Raj Kapoor's father," Karan says. One day, when someone looking for a partner to start a duty-free business in India asked the younger Kapoor for references, the actor simply pointed them to his neighbours.

"My uncle, Viren, was a major businessman at the time, and asked my dad if he wanted to do it and, of course, my father was more than happy to," adds Karan. With the first and only investment of Rs.42 lakh from his uncle, the business took off, starting with Trivandrum airport in 2003, before creating a pan-India footprint by 2008. Karan joined the business in 2012 after graduating in business from Poddar College of Commerce and Economics in Mumbai.

In the last 14 years, working with his father has been a richer education in management, risk mitigation and crisis handling for Karan than any B-school degree could have taught him. Add to this hands-on experience, his passion, business acumen, and disciplined focus (each day of the week has a fixed cadence for him unless he is travelling, Karan says), and Cococart's journey, from being a website selling chocolates to scaling to a multi-million dollar omnichannel business with 65 stores around the country (and 30 plus in the pipeline), begins to add up. They are available on Blinkit too.

At the same time, Cococart, like most businesses, isn't immune from volatility. The war in West Asia sent cocoa prices soaring, air traffic has been hit due to prohibitively expensive fares and scarcity of aviation fuel, while shipments have been delayed by the stalemate over the Strait of Hormuz. The Toblerone bar, an evergreen hit with duty-free shoppers, now retails at around Rs.399, from Rs.199 in 2020.

"We had reached about 15,000 daily traffic at Navi Mumbai airport in May, but now (September) we are down to 4,000," Karan says. "Even Mumbai airport traffic is down by 16%." The setback in airport sales, however, has not deterred him from clocking several impressive wins. "Our direct e-commerce brings only 1% of the revenue, but quick commerce now contributes about 30%," he adds. "As for the retail and distribution businesses, each brings about Rs.15 crore a month." Despite this robust form, it isn't all a numbers game. Rather, Karan has his eyes trained on the longer-term, which has led him to forge a flurry of exclusive partnerships.

Last year, Cococart acquired the rights to distribute Venchi, an Italian chocolate and gelato brand, as well as Neuhaus, a luxury Belgian chocolate manufacturer, in India. Other additions include Vapiano, Cafe Bateel and Le Pain Quotidien. While these brands have added heft to Cococart's premium portfolio, their products are expensive, especially for a price-sensitive market like India.

"Venchi sells at around €6.50 a scoop in Italy, its cheapest market, which means it translates to roughly Rs.700 for India, which simply doesn't work," says Karan. "So we have priced it at Rs.495, even though we are paying 110% import duty. We are okay to take a margin hit and play the long game because we love the brand very much." This high-risk, high-reward strategy shapes his decision-making in other aspects of the business too.

"Every first order of any brand is made by me because otherwise the learning curve is too long," Karan says. "Most confectionery companies have huge portfolios, that's why I go wide on the initial order. So, if I know I'm going to be able to buy only eight products from Hershey's Malaysia, I'll order at least 20-25 and let the customer decide which ones stay." With all the margin pressure and expiry dates, he is well aware that some of the products may have to be liquidated. That's why he underwrites the first order. From the second time, it's the team's responsibility to make things work.

Aside from taking such bets, Cococart is no less adventurous about owning a distinct identity for itself. In 2023, it launched Rhine Valley Gourmet, its own chocolate brand, inspired by "the best of European chocolate making methods", as the website puts it. Rhine Valley offers a wide array of flavours, all devoid of palm oil-the products contribute 12-14% of total sales.

Even though Rhine Valley has strong competition in the form of Lindt and Toblerone, Karan isn't willing to compromise on pricing. "Our benchmark was Lindt when it came to pricing, but we felt our chocolate was superior in every way.

We use a far higher-grade and concentration of nuts, for instance," he claims. "So we decided to launch it at Rs.495 a bar, about 20% more premium than Lindt, which was averaging at Rs.400 a bar at the time." Cococart's aspiration was to deliver a homegrown chocolate that tasted as good as a Laderach or Sprungli (a bar of these premium brands costs Rs.1,500- Rs.2,000), but at half the price. And Karan came up with a strategy to make it work.

"We've been doing confectionery and travel retail for long enough to know that if a pricey product is on offer, its cumulative sales value will still be large," he says. "So we had a 2+1 or 3+1 offer all year, though now, with cocoa prices on the rise, we can't run similar deals anymore."

In terms of stocking brands, Cococart's advantage has been the large dataset available to it from years of selling duty-free confectionery. "We established our core with the six 'global giants'-Lindt, Ferrero Rocher, Mondelez, Mars, Hershey's and Nestle," says Karan. "However, there were lots of learnings and eye-openers."

The UK variant of KitKat, for instance, never took off in India despite its popularity here because no one wanted to pay even Rs.79 for the two-finger bar (the Indian version costs Rs.15). "Nestle's After Eight didn't sell at all in the duty-free business but remains a best-selling product in the domestic market for Cococart," he offers as another example.

Being on top of the shifting dynamics of demand and supply, decoding customer behaviour, and pivoting quickly to address new challenges keep the business agile and exciting for him. But the real drive comes from deep within. "If I decide to do something, I can't do it half-heartedly," he says. "And I hate losing."

data.title: RBI tightens forex derivatives framework to ensure orderly functioning of market
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday announced a host of restrictive measures relating specifically to foreign exchange (forex) derivatives contracts even as it opened a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) in view of the evolving conditions and to ensure orderly functioning of the forex market.

This comes in the backdrop of the rupee weakening against the US dollar and may be aimed at staving off the possibility of the rupee breaching the 97 mark against the US dollar.

As part of the restrictive measures relating specifically to forex (fx) derivatives, the central bank said Authorised Dealers/ AD (Banks authorised to deal in forex) cannot permit users to rebook any forex derivative contract involving INR (Rupee).

Such forex derivative contracts, whether deliverable or non-deliverable, will include those that have been cancelled with any Authorised Dealer after the issuance of the Directions. Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity shall continue to be permitted, subject to compliance with the extant regulatory provisions.

The existing threshold of $100 million equivalent for undertaking forex derivative transactions to hedge contracted exposures without establishing the existence of the underlying exposure has been reduced to $5 million equivalent, across all ADs.

The corresponding threshold for taking positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving INR, without establishing the existence of underlying exposure, has also been reduced from $100 million to $5 million equivalent, across all Recognised Stock Exchanges taken together.

RBI said ADs will be required to obtain and retain an undertaking from users entering into forex derivative contracts involving INR to hedge contracted exposures, confirming that the same underlying exposure has not been hedged with any other Authorised Dealer.

Maintain Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve

In respect of all fx derivative contracts involving INR that are for notional value exceeding $2 million equivalent, AD is required to maintain with the Reserve Bank an Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) in cash, equal to 20 per cent of the INR equivalent of the notional amount of each transaction. T

This FERR is applicable for ffx derivative contracts involving INR undertaken to hedge current account exposures where the user purchases foreign currency against the INR.

V Rama Chandra Reddy, Head - Treasury, Karur Vysya Bank, said introducing a 20 per cent cash Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) on specified transactions exceeding $2 million will Impose an additional liquidity cost on covered transactions and discourage excessive positions.

He opined that the central objective appears to be curbing excessive speculative positions, preventing duplicate hedging of the same exposure and ensuring that foreign exchange derivatives are used primarily for genuine risk management.

“While banks may face higher compliance and liquidity costs, customers undertaking genuine hedging may experience additional documentation and some repricing. The measures could moderate speculative activity and promote orderly market conditions.

“It would therefore be more credible to say the measures may help moderate excessive positioning rather than claim that they will necessarily strengthen the currency. The rupee will continue to be influenced by global factors and underlying dollar demand and supply,” Reddy said.

Dollar window for oil companies

Meanwhile, on the basis of assessment of current market conditions, RBI has decided to open a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) -- Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Bharat Petroleum Corporation.

Under the facility, the central bank will undertake sale of USD to the public sector OMCs through designated bank/s. The facility will come in effect from October 12, 2026 and will remain in place until further notice.

data.title: Egypt Inflation Rate at 7-Month Low of 13.9%
data.description:
Egypt's annual urban inflation eased for the second straight month to 13.9% in September 2026 from 14.5% in August. It was the lowest inflation rate since February, as the impact of higher fuel prices continued to fade, with transport inflation slowing slightly to 24.3% in September from 24.4% in August, while housing and utilities inflation moderated to 35.2% from 42.8%.

Egypt raised fuel prices in early March by about 14% to 17% across a wide range of petroleum products, marking the first increase this year amid elevated global oil prices.

Inflation also moderated for clothing and footwear (13.9% vs 14.0% in August), health (4.5% vs 4.6%), and alcoholic beverages and narcotics (8.3% vs 9.1%).

Meanwhile, inflation accelerated for food and beverages (7.2% vs 6.3% in August) and furnishings (17.7% vs 16.9%).

On a monthly basis, the CPI rose 1.3%, after edging up 0.1% in the previous month, marking the fastest increase in four months.

data.title: 'India has lowest data prices, lowest cost payment systems': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu responds to Elon Musk
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has responded to Elon Musk's criticism of India's regulatory framework for satellite internet services, citing the country's low mobile data prices, affordable medicines and low-cost digital payment systems to argue that competition has benefited consumers.

In a post on X, Vembu defended the role of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani's Jio in bringing down data prices and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government had encouraged competition and the growth of startups.

"These are the facts Elon," Vembu wrote, responding to the Tesla and SpaceX CEO's remarks about Starlink's entry into India and alleged monopolistic practices.

Vembu argued that India offers some of the world's lowest data prices, pointing to the widespread use of dual-SIM smartphones and large mobile data plans.

"India has the among the lowest data prices in the world. It is so good that I don't even bother to connect to local Wifi when I travel in India and just tether my phone to work on my computer. Indians routinely have dual SIM phones with large data plans because they are so affordable. Ambani's launch of Jio is directly responsible for the low data prices Indians enjoy.

India has among the lowest drug prices in the world (and going lower still). People who visit India buy medicines to take home quite regularly now.

India has among the lowest cost payment systems in the world in UPI.

On the other hand, Tesla is protected from Chinese competition in the US market, keeping EV prices higher in America than elsewhere.

Prime Minister Modi has worked hard to create a competitive economy where the benefits flow to the average Indian. His government does not tolerate monopolies. He has also actively promoted and encouraged a massive surge in startups and that is the best signal of a highly competitive economy.

Directly due to Modi government policy, Indian startups are making major advances in low cost rockets and that poses a threat to SpaceX the same say the Chinese EVs threaten Tesla.

These are the facts Elon."

Vembu's remarks came after Musk questioned whether Indian business interests were preventing Starlink from entering the country's satellite communications market.

Musk, in a post on X on Wednesday, alleged that Starlink was being blocked in India by certain business interests.

"Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. This is a crime against the people of India!" the tech mogul wrote.

On Thursday, Musk again questioned the delay in Starlink receiving a licence to operate in India, claiming that the company had complied with the government's requirements.

"Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he wrote.

Musk subsequently took another swipe at Mukesh Ambani, sarcastically referring to him as India's prime minister while questioning the role of business interests in Starlink's entry into the country.

"Dear Prime Minister Ambani, please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO wrote.

"Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" he asked, adding, "There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better."

In his Friday post, Musk also argued that Starlink had helped save lives during natural disasters when other communications systems failed. He said allowing the company to operate in India could similarly help save men, women and children across the country.

The Ministry of Communications rejected the allegations in a statement issued on Thursday morning, calling the claim baseless.

"A post is being circulated on social media regarding the fairness of India's regulatory framework for satellite communication services and suggesting that it is being applied in a discriminatory manner. The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services," it said.

The government also said the security assessment required for satellite communication services was underway.

Starlink, owned by SpaceX, is among three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services that have been granted telecom licences by the Centre.

The other two are Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio Satellite Communications Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Jio Platforms.

However, receiving a telecom licence does not by itself allow the companies to begin offering services. They must also demonstrate compliance with security conditions before spectrum can be assigned and commercial operations can begin.

The Centre has said the security assessment, which forms part of this process, is underway.

The dispute has brought attention to the regulatory approvals required for satellite internet services in India, as well as competing claims over market access, consumer choice and competition in the telecommunications sector.

data.title: Markets Espresso: Tere bhi din aayenge chote, accha khaasa hil jainga
data.description:
Hello there, Espresso Lovers. Relieved that the weekend is here? You bet we are. With the kind of week that went by, one could only count down to the weekend, which, with absolute certainty, will feel like it went past by the time you finish reading this episode!

Mereko to aisa Dhak Dhak ho rela tha when the first ticks of the indicative closing price flashed on Friday during the Closing Auction Session. They were below 22,421, the level the Nifty needed to close above to prevent a ninth straight weekly loss. A cat has nine lives; the Nifty does not need nine red weekly candles for sure! While we sat before our screens, just the way we wait for India to win the World Cup final, the heavens chose to have some mercy on the bulls. It was a weekly gain. Even if it was just 100 points, even if it was short-covering, a dead-cat bounce, whatever, it was a green tick. And as we say in cricketing terminology, inside edge or outside edge, it still went to the boundary. We'll take it.

At the end of every family drama Hindi film, it is the proverbial Khota Sikka (black sheep) that turns out to be the hero and the knight in shining armour. Indian IT stocks have been the same Khota Sikka for our markets in 2026. Beaten out of shape, they led the market gains on Friday, ensuring that a green candle appeared on the Nifty chart. TCS' results infused some sense of optimism. It turned out to be the "no bad news is good news" kind of quarter. Adding to the optimism was the sell-off in AI stocks on Wall Street after OpenAI's revenue disclosure fell short of expectations. The street liked it, and for one day, every other headwind was forgotten. Who are we to complain!

Happy, emotional music started playing in the background, similar to the one in a Hindi film when a mother found her long-lost child after 25 years, when Trent reported 23% revenue growth in its provisional business update for the quarter. Quarter after Quarter of delivering revenue growth that disappointed the street, which left no mercy in bashing the stock after every business update, the 23% number indeed felt as if it had come after 25 years! For a change, the stock was up 12% the following day and ended the week as the third-best Nifty 500 performer. We'll stop short of using the "FORM IS TEMPORARY, CLASS IS PERMANENT" analogy simply because this should not be a one-off. When consistency comes, analogy will follow, ma broda! Analogy kahaan jaane wali hai! Still a beaten-down stock, still away from 52-week highs, well away from record highs, the Trent bulls would now hope that it finally clicks to deliver all-round performance, thereby taking the stock back to its previous days of glory. That's our stock of the week!

Once upon a time, there was a character named Shehenshah, who was rishte me sabka baap, made his own laws, caught criminals himself, heard their cases himself, and punished them himself too. And then there is Donald Trump. The biggest proponent of the odd-even scheme, and he doesn't even live in New Delhi! On an odd day, he says no deal with Iran; on an even day, he says we are having "productive negotiations" with them. One day he will bash Russia; the next day, strike a deal with them to buy their oil and diesel. Wait a minute! Did they not pass a "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026?" that allowed him to impose tariffs of as much as 100% on countries that brought Russian oil and their products? So will President Trump impose tariffs on the US as well? Is the US now going to be funding Russia's war machine, as many countries, including India, have been accused of? We would love to see the Administration defend this one. Many memes loading. Brace yourselves.

Jefferies is starting to favour largecaps over the broader markets because the risk-reward appears more favourable. Unfortunately, there has only been risk, with barely any reward for a largecap investor over the last few years. The index, from its September 2024 peak, is down, most of the stocks have delivered negative returns, and some relentless FII selling continues to pressure these names time and again.

During Editor's Playbook on Friday, we were trying to decode whether HRITHIK will dance again. Back in the day, the HRITHIK stock portfolio was a well-known market acronym comprising HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, ICICI Bank, TCS, Hindustan Unilever, ITC and Kotak Mahindra Bank. But just as our OG Hrithik has delivered one dud after another in recent times, the HRITHIK stock portfolio has been a dud too. A film that hit the theatres at 9 AM on Friday and was pulled down by 3 PM. Many years, zero returns. HDFC Bank down 11% in the last five years, HUL down 30%, TCS down 45%, Kotak up 13%, ITC up 15%. The only one that has stood out here is ICICI Bank, which is up 90%.

Everybody has had a rough time trying to remain convinced about investing in largecaps. Valuations have corrected. Most of these stocks are trading below their historical averages. In an ideal time, these would be what analysts call "Screaming BUYS". But we live in times that are anything but ideal. Still no buyers for them. HRITHIK is still struggling. And since HRITHIK commands a significant weightage on the Nifty, the index is struggling too. This is not only a test of investor patience, but also a test of analysts who continue to ascribe "buy" ratings on them with lofty price targets. HDFC Bank is still a near-consensus "buy". M&M, which is at a 52-week low, has no "sell" ratings. 90% of the analysts who track Maruti, also at a 52-week low, have a "buy" rating on it. Investors should also start a Make HRITHIK Dance Again campaign, maybe then the tide turns for them!

You may want to keep watching Geopolitics, but the real market mover has arrived again. It's EARNINGS TIME BABY! And contrary to the first quarter, where there were absolutely zero expectations and the results turned out to be 1 to 1.5 or even 2 versus the zero expectations, this time around, there are expectations. That results will be good. There will be healthy topline growth; there will be healthy profitability growth. However, margins may be under pressure, as we saw in the case of TCS, but that might also be on a case-by-case basis. The problem of expectations is that when you fall short of them, the punishment is a severe one these days. Earnings miss ki sazaa milegi. Barabar milegi. We know the drill.

TCS has set the ball rolling with the IT results, and the onus is now on Wipro, HCLTech, Tech Mahindra and Persistent Systems to justify the optimism that TCS has infused in the minds of investors, that it is not doomsday for Indian IT afterall. It may take time, but they'll find their own niche in a world obsessed with AI. Besides these, HDB Financial, Bajaj Consumer, CEAT, ICICI Lombard, Karur Vysya Bank, Nestle India, among many others, will also be declaring their results. And then, of course, comes SUPER SATURDAY again when every bank decides in unison to report results. For now, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Yes Bank are on the list along with some other non-bank lenders. Don't be surprised if more get added to this list. We're ready. You'll get ready too!

To all the largecap and stock market investors who have not made much or have lost money during the last two years, we know it has been painful, we know it hurts, we know it has been a test, but while it is easy to throw in the towel, courage and optimism also comes with a price. Just as the good times don't last forever, the bad times won't last forever either. And what better song to summarise this than this one, which was the anthem of us boys during school days - "Fatela Jeb Sil Jayega, Jo Chahega Mil Jayega, Tere Din Bhi Aayenge Chote, Accha Khasa Hil Jainga. Rukneka Nahi, Thakneka Nahi, Life Me Chalte Rehneka!" Whether this is to comfort the underperforming largecaps or to those who are still invested in them, it goes both ways.

It's time for Durga Puja, and we can only pray to Maa Durga that the Mahishasura of losses sees its Vadh at the earliest and the bleeding portfolios turn green again! We'll see you next week, but on SUNDAY this time because of our Super Saturday. So do like, share and subscribe to our Espresso and follow us on our Social Media Handles! Until then, lights will guide us home!

data.title: India remains key market for global smartphone makers amid evolving demand, component price pressure
data.description:
Global smartphone manufacturers view India as an essential, high-growth market that continues to sustain demand despite escalating prices of core components like memory and storage. Speaking to ANI on the sidelines of the Qualcomm event at the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 at Yashobhoomi, leaders from Xiaomi, Motorola and iQOO underscored that Indian consumers are maturing rapidly, shifting preference toward advanced processing platforms and experience-led devices.

Gautam Batra, Associate Director – Product Marketing at Xiaomi, noted that consumer appetite remains resilient even as raw material expenses drive retail price adjustments across the industry.“I think the prices are going up for, whether it's RAM, whether it's storage, and in turn the devices prices are also going up. I think the market is now aware it's been a long trend. It's not just a recent thing; it has been ongoing, and the market has now recalibrated according to it, and we see a good demand coming in even now,” Batra told ANI.

Highlighting the country’s weight in Xiaomi’s global portfolio, Batra stated that the domestic user base remains highly aspirational. “India is of course a big market for us and for a lot of smartphone makers, OEMs and of course it is an aspirational market,” Batra said.

“The Indian market is a huge big deal for us and of course a much faster growing market as well.” Detailing product roadmaps, Batra announced that the newly unveiled Xiaomi 18 Pro flagship will feature the newly announced Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 platform across international and Indian channels to deliver upgraded graphics, photography, and artificial intelligence performance.

Echoing this focus on consumer evolution, Shivam Ranjan, Marketing Head - APAC at Motorola, stated that Indian buyers are recalibrating how they evaluate handsets, placing greater emphasis on usability rather than isolated component data. “I think India as a market has been constantly evolving over a period of time. We are seeing consumers becoming more mature, moving beyond just hard specifications or hardware specifications to now demanding experiences that are human centric and human first,” Ranjan said.

Ranjan previewed Motorola's upcoming Signature 27 handset, scheduled for rollout in 2026 as one of the earliest models powered by the Snapdragon 6 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. He noted that the device integrates camera features, agentic AI, and hardware design aimed at addressing modern user requirements.Meanwhile, iQOO announced its forthcoming flagship device, the iQOO 16, built around Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 platform.

“Today we have announced the launch of iQOO 16, which is going to be our latest and the fastest smartphone ever. This is going to launch in India very soon,” said Nipun Marya, CEO, iQOO, adding that further collaborative details with the chipset provider will be disclosed subsequently.
